“The transition of RRFS from research to operations represents a major step towards modernizing NOAA’s weather forecast modeling suite,” said NOAA Administrator Neil Jacobs, Ph.D. “RRFS extends the reach of some of our best capabilities and delivers more accurate, earlier forecasts to support Americans’ safety and security.” The RRFS combines the hourly updates of NOAA’s short-term High Resolution Rapid Refresh Model (HRRR) and its ability to issue forecasts for each 3-kilometer by 3-kilometer square of land surface with the larger, continental domain of the North American Mesoscale model (NAM). The RRFS also extends forecast lead time for the contiguous United States to 84 hours, compared with the HRRR’s 48 hours. RRFS covers all of North America including Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico, along with Canada, Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean with enough detail to predict high-impact, small-scale events such as thunderstorms, tornadoes and flash floods. RRFS also features seamless predictions for coastal and offshore areas that previously required forecasters to switch between different weather models.
